neighbours.label: a past participle or predicate adjective after 'that was' or 'was' in a story's first-event clause (was sent, was ready)
fire: The first letter that was sent from the fort never arrived.
The first apple that was ready to pick was small and sour.
The first radio message was sent from a ship near Cuba.
The first room that was ready to paint was the kitchen.
The first report was sent from Boston in the early hours.
The first loaf that was ready to eat went to the baker's son.
The first telegram was sent from Washington to Baltimore.
The first house that was ready to sell had a red door.
quiet: The first letter from the fort never arrived at all.
The first apple on the small tree looked sour.
The first radio station in Cuba played dance music.
The first room on the left has a large kitchen.
The first report from Boston came in the early hours.
The first loaf of the day went to the baker's son.
The first telegraph line ran from Washington to Baltimore.
The first house on the street had a red door.
